title: LLMjacking now targets cloud billing accounts, not only API keys
dek: Attackers linked their own projects to compromised victims' billing accounts and ran large volumes of AI inference outside victims' logging scope.
evidence: Wiz incident-response research from multiple investigated cases
takeaway: Monitor billing-account membership and cross-project attachments as first-class AI abuse indicators.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: Cloud projects can charge a central billing account even when their workloads and logs are invisible to the payer.

paragraphs: Billing is a trust boundary: Cloud projects can charge a central billing account even when their workloads and logs are invisible to the payer.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: Wiz observed attackers phish GCP admins, relax domain restrictions, grant billing roles to outsider accounts and attach attacker-owned projects to victim billing accounts.
The malicious inference runs in foreign projects. Rotating keys in the victim's own project does not remove the rogue project's billing attachment.

paragraphs: Cross-tenant LLMjacking: Wiz observed attackers phish GCP admins, relax domain restrictions, grant billing roles to outsider accounts and attach attacker-owned projects to victim billing accounts.
Why API-key rotation fails: The malicious inference runs in foreign projects. Rotating keys in the victim's own project does not remove the rogue project's billing attachment.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: Wiz reports investigated victims incurring tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars in unauthorized Gemini API charges in 24–48 hours; case reports are not a typical-loss estimate.
The victim sees costs but does not automatically see the attacker's prompt and model-output logs, because execution takes place in projects it does not own.

paragraphs: Incident magnitude: Wiz reports investigated victims incurring tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars in unauthorized Gemini API charges in 24–48 hours; case reports are not a typical-loss estimate.
Detection gap: The victim sees costs but does not automatically see the attacker's prompt and model-output logs, because execution takes place in projects it does not own.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: Alert on external billing admins, cross-project billing links, domain-policy changes and unexpected model API enablement.
Detach unauthorized projects, revoke billing roles and remediate compromised identities; spend caps alone may be too slow.

paragraphs: Monitor billing relationships: Alert on external billing admins, cross-project billing links, domain-policy changes and unexpected model API enablement.
Contain the right asset: Detach unauthorized projects, revoke billing roles and remediate compromised identities; spend caps alone may be too slow.
